subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: Should OpenClaw expose a Gateway-level global auth-refresh operation that preserves active session context, and if so what session scope and administrator authorization contract should it use?
rationale: The existing reset operation is intentionally session-scoped and destructive to session continuity; choosing a global credential-rebind capability determines public protocol semantics, security boundaries, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Design an additive global refresh
options.body: Add an admin-scoped auth-refresh operation with explicit all-active or selected-session scope, preserving session identity and transcript state.

options.title: Keep session refresh manual
options.body: Retain single-session reset behavior and document that auth changes require per-session recovery until a supported lifecycle contract is sponsored.

options.title: Fold into provider switching
options.body: Make global session refresh part of a future provider-switch transaction rather than exposing a separate Gateway action.

recommendation.title: Design an additive global refresh
recommendation.body: Add an admin-scoped auth-refresh operation with explicit all-active or selected-session scope, preserving session identity and transcript state.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and the latest maintainer-facing review place this person closest to the Gateway/session lifecycle contract.
